grades.reason: This passage introduces race conditions with a sellTicket example. It says nothing about monitors, condition waiting, or how they combine with mutual exclusion.

grades.quote:
Section 4.3.2 presents an alternative, more structured

interface to mutexes, known as monitors.
grades.reason: This is an introduction to mutexes and monitors. It says monitors are a more structured interface to mutexes, which gives limited context. It does not explain how a monitor combines exclusion with waiting for a condition, and condition variables are not mentioned.

grades.quote: If more than one thread is trying to lock the same mutex, only one of them will switch the mutex from unlocked to locked; that thread will be allowed to proceed. The others will wait until the mutex is again unlocked. This behavior of the lock operation provides mutual exclusion.
grades.reason: Explains mutex locking and how it provides mutual exclusion, which is only the exclusion half of a monitor. It never discusses monitors or condition waiting, so it gives limited background.

grades.quote: One, condition variables, is an important extension to monitors; the combination of monitors with condition variables allows many situations to be cleanly handled.
grades.reason: This is a chapter overview. It says monitors provide mutual exclusion and that condition variables extend monitors, so the two combine. It doesn't explain how a monitor does this.
